step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a fully integrated differential active filter stage, likely part of the baseband channel-select filter (e.g., Chebyshev or all-pass section) for a W-CDMA receiver. It features a bipolar differential pair (Q3, Q10) with emitter follower buffers, AC-coupled inputs, and cross-coupled capacitors to synthesize the required filter poles.

paper_reference.title: Fully Integrated W-CDMA IF Receiver and IF Transmitter Including IF Synthesizer and On-Chip VCO for UMTS Mobiles

DC_Power.description: Total DC power consumption of the filter stage.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly isolated for this sub-block

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming Vcc=1.8V. The circuit has multiple current branches (tail current Q9, emitter followers Q2, Q6, Q12, Q13, and current sources Q5, Q8). Assuming ~1mA per branch with 1k bias resistors, total current is ~5-6mA. Power = 1.8V * 5.5mA = 9.9mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on standard biasing for high-frequency bipolar active filters to maintain sufficient gm and bandwidth.

Low_Freq_Gain.description: Differential voltage gain at low frequencies (passband).

sky130_expected.calculation: Diff pair (Q3, Q10) tail current ~1mA -> Ic = 0.5mA. gm = Ic/Vt = 0.5mA / 26mV = 19.2 mA/V. With assumed 1k load resistors (R5, R11), Gain = gm * R_load = 19.2. In dB: 20*log10(19.2) = 25.6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain is heavily dependent on the chosen load resistors and tail current. 25 dB is typical for an active filter gain stage.

Gain_1_92MHz.description: Voltage gain at the W-CDMA baseband channel edge (1.92 MHz).

sky130_expected.calculation: With assumed C=10pF and R=1k, the dominant pole is around 1 / (2*pi*1k*10p) = 15.9 MHz. At 1.92 MHz, the gain should be nearly identical to the low-frequency gain, with minimal attenuation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: 1.92 MHz is well within the passband of the W-CDMA channel select filter.

Transient_Swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing for a given input.

sky130_expected.calculation: With an input amplitude of 0.1V and a gain of ~19 V/V, the theoretical output is 1.9V. However, the supply is 1.8V, so the output will clip. The maximum linear swing is limited by Vcc and Vce(sat), typically around 1.2Vpp differential.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Limited by the 1.8V supply and the headroom required for the tail current source and load resistors.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC frequency response (passband and channel edge gain), and transient output swing of the active filter. Missing component values (R, C) have been populated with typical values to allow simulation.
step3_testbench.spice:
* W-CDMA Baseband Filter Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Generic BJT model to support the extracted 'npn' instances
.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100 vaf=50)

* Supplies and Biases
Vcc Vcc 0 1.8
VVBIAS Vbias 0 1.2
Vbias2 N10 0 0.8
Vbias3 N21 0 0.8
Vbias4 N23 0 0.8
Vbias5 N18 0 0.8

* AC and Transient Inputs (AC coupled)
Vinp in_p 0 dc 0 ac 1 sin(0 0.01 1Meg)
Vinn in_n 0 dc 0 ac -1 sin(0 -0.01 1Meg)
Cin1 in_p N1 1u
Cin2 in_n N3 1u

* Differential Output VCVS for easy measurement
Ediff out_diff 0 out outx 1

* DUT (with added typical values for R and C to enable simulation)
Q1 N20 Vbias N22 npn
Q2 Vcc N9 out npn
R6 N19 GND 1k
Q3 N9 N5 N16 npn
Q5 N12 N23 N19 npn
R2 N22 GND 1k
Q4 Vcc N18 N11 npn
Q6 Vcc N8 outx npn
Q7 outx N15 N0 npn
Q8 N2 N21 N13 npn
R3 Vcc N20 1k
R4 N14 GND 1k
R5 Vcc N9 1k
R10 N11 GND 1k
R7 N13 GND 1k
Q9 N16 N10 N14 npn
R9 N15 GND 1k
R8 N0 GND 1k
Q10 N8 N4 N16 npn
Q11 out N14 N15 npn
R1 N5 Vcc 10k
Q12 Vcc N1 N12 npn
R11 Vcc N8 1k
Q13 Vcc N3 N2 npn
R12 N3 N20 10k
C1 N1 N3 5p
R13 N4 Vcc 10k
R14 N1 N20 10k
C2 N3 N1 5p
C3 N2 N5 10p
C4 N1 GND 5p
C5 N3 GND 5p
C6 N4 N12 10p

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(Vcc) * 1.8
print power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 20 10k 100Meg
let gain_db = vdb(out_diff)
meas ac gain_100k find gain_db at=100k
meas ac gain_1_92M find gain_db at=1.92Meg
meas ac gain_10M find gain_db at=10Meg

* Transient Analysis
tran 10n 5u
meas tran vout_max max v(out_diff)
meas tran vout_min min v(out_diff)
let vout_pp = vout_max - vout_min
print vout_pp

quit
.endc
